title: Schema Gateway: ergonomics for function invocation, streaming resume, and retry profiles
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Motivation: customers use SDK helpers to declare functions/tool schemas and invoke them from model responses. We need a cross-language 'Schema Gateway' utility in the SDKs that validates model-provided arguments, applies safe coercion rules, and orchestration helpers for invoking functions with robust retry semantics and streaming resume. Current ad-hoc patterns cause inconsistent behavior across Python/TS/Go: some SDKs silently coerce types, others throw; streaming interruptions lose in-flight state; retries are either too aggressive for non-idempotent tools or too conservative for simple ops. This ticket defines and implements ergonomic primitives and examples across the three SDKs so developers can rely on consistent safety, observability, and performance.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unified schema validation utility available in Python/TS/Go with same high-level config flags (mode: strict|lenient|coerce; max_depth; whitelist of allowed fields).
- Validation emits structured diagnostics with stable error codes for developer-facing errors and telemetry.
- Invocation helper provides: idempotency header support, per-call retry profile (idempotent|non-idempotent|stream-resume), exponential jittered backoff, max attempts, and circuit-breaker hooks.
- Streaming API supports checkpointed resume using opaque resume tokens and verifies KV-cache position on resume to prevent duplicate side-effects.
- Comprehensive examples in each SDK: decorator/wrapper in Python, typed helper in TS (Promise/AsyncIterator friendly), and context-aware client in Go.
- E2E tests that simulate transient 5xx, permanent 4xx, and partial-stream failures showing correct retry behavior and no double-invokes for non-idempotent ops.
- Docs and migration guide published in the SDK repo and referenced from the platform docs.
- Benchmarks: no more than 5% median latency regression for typical short tool calls when validation enabled in lenient mode.
technical_notes:
Design principles: explicitness, predictable safety, minimal runtime overhead.
Validation: use a small, deterministic schema subset (compatible with JSON Schema draft-07) implemented as a runtime-optimized validator per language. Offer two presets: strict (reject mismatches) and lenient (coerce basic types: number<->string, null->absent) with an explicit opt-in for deep coercions. Provide transform hooks so customers can supply a post-validate mapper.
Invocation helpers: separate concerns - validation, transport, and retry orchestration. Retry profiles map to semantic intent (idempotent, safe-retry, stream-resume). For idempotent calls, include an Idempotency-Key header and allow retries until success; for non-idempotent calls default to single try unless caller sets retry policy. Retry decisions based on normalized error codes: transient (HTTP 429, 502, 503, 504, request timeouts) vs permanent (4xx client errors).
Streaming resume: persist minimal opaque resume tokens server-side (we store sequence IDs) and encode a short HMAC to bind token to caller and function signature. Client resume flow: on streaming disconnect, fetch token, re-open stream with resume token and a 'resume-checkpoint' that validates last-acknowledged event id. Resume must be gated by validation mode to avoid replaying side-effects for non-idempotent functions.
Language ergonomics: Python exposes a decorator @function_schema(..., mode='lenient') that returns a callable wrapper handling validation & retry; TypeScript exposes a typed helper createFunctionInvoker<TArgs, TResult>(schema, opts) returning invoke(args) and streamInvoke(args) with AsyncIterable support; Go exposes an Invoker type with Invoke(ctx, args, opts) and StreamInvoke(ctx, args, opts) patterns and uses context for timeouts/cancellation.
Telemetry: emit events: validation.failure, invoke.attempt, invoke.retry, invoke.success, stream.resume, stream.resume-failed with stable tags (sdk_lang, schema_hash, retry_profile). Avoid logging user PII/args in plain-text — provide scrubbed/minimal diagnostics.
implementation_plan: 1) Spec RFC: finalize JSON Schema subset, retry profile enums, and resume token format (owner: Marco). 2) Shared test corpus: canonical schemas and fuzz cases (owner: Samir). 3) Python implementation (owner: Priya): decorator + integration tests + example. 4) TypeScript implementation (owner: Marco): typed helper + AsyncIterator example + docs. 5) Go implementation (owner: Hyejin): Invoker type + context-aware stream resume + tests. 6) Platform hooks: lightweight server resume token API and HMAC key rotation support (coord with infra team). 7) Release notes, migration guide, and SDK examples repo updates.
test_plan:
- Unit: validator permutations (strict/lenient/coerce) across 1000 schema cases; error-code assertions.
- Integration: mock backend to simulate transient errors and verify retry counters, idempotency header presence, and no duplicate side-effects.
- Streaming: simulate dropped TCP mid-stream and verify resume flow with valid and tampered tokens.
- Fuzz: random type mismatches and extra fields to ensure validator doesn't crash.
- Performance: run 10k short calls with validation disabled/enabled (lenient) and measure p50/p95 latency and CPU overhead.
- Docs test: code samples compile in TS and Go; Python examples pass lint and unit checks.
